tool_input.description: Add CSRF priming to profile tests

result:
All checks pass: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 6/6 passing, `guren check` 0 failures.

`ProfileController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts`) was reading the request body raw via `this.request.json<ProfileInput>()` and writing it with `User.forceUpdate()`, which skipped both Zod validation and the model's fillable allowlist — so any field in the payload (`id`, `passwordHash`, …) landed in the account row. I restored it to validate with the already-present `ProfileUpdateSchema` from `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts` (name required/trimmed/≤120, email required and well-formed, lowercased, optional password of at least 8 characters where empty means "keep current") via `this.validateBody()`, which throws a 422 the profile form renders per-field, and to persist through `User.update({ id: user.id }, { name, email, ...(password ? { password } : {}) })` so only the profile's own fields are written and the password is hashed by `AuthenticatableModel` as on registration. The Zod object strips unknown keys before the update, so extra fields are ignored while the valid ones still save. I added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts` covering the malformed email, empty name, and short password rejections (asserting the record is unchanged), plus a valid update that ignores injected `id`/`passwordHash` and stores the email lowercased; the tests prime session/CSRF with `withCsrf()` since the real app mounts CSRF middleware.
